## 0) The rule of the month (keeps everything coherent)
**Only one “Main Project” is allowed to receive deep work time.**  
Everything else is maintenance.

If you want, reply with what your one project is (one sentence), and I’ll help you slice it into a clean plan.

## 1) What each app is for (clear roles = fewer decisions)
### Apple Notes = thinking + plan + reference
- project brief, outlines, research, drafts, meeting notes, “what’s next”
- a single place to see the project end‑to‑end

### Apple Reminders = executable actions
- only next actions and small steps (verbs)
- your daily shortlist comes from here

### Google Calendar = time + reality
- time blocks, appointments, deadlines
- protects deep work from the chaos of an inconsistent schedule

---

## 2) One-time setup (15–25 minutes)

### A) Apple Notes: create a “Main Project Hub” note
In Notes, create a folder: **Projects**

### B) Apple Reminders: create a small list structure
Create these lists:

1. **Today (Shortlist)**  
2. **Main Project**  
3. **Admin / Life** (everything else)  
4. **Waiting / Blocked**

### C) Google Calendar: two reusable blocks (anchors)
Because your schedule is inconsistent, don’t try to schedule a perfect day. Use **anchors**.

Create two “event templates” (just recurring events you can move/delete as needed):

1) **Daily Deep Work (45–90 min)**

- Title: `Deep Work — Main Project`  
- Description: link to your pinned Notes “Main Project Hub” (paste the note link if you want—Notes lets you “Share” -> copy link, or just a keyword like the exact note title).

2) **Daily Reset (10 min)**  
- Put it near end of day or after dinner.  
- Title: `Reset — Plan tomorrow`

If a day explodes, you move the Deep Work block instead of abandoning it.

---

## 3) The daily operating system (the smallest set of habits that works)

### Morning (3 minutes): “Pick the day”
In Reminders:
1) Open **Main Project** list.
2) Choose **one** “Most Important Next Action” (MINA).  
   - Must be doable in **45–90 minutes**.
3) Put that MINA into **Today (Shortlist)**.
4) Add 0–2 extra small tasks max.

That’s it. No long planning.

---

### Deep work block: “One tab, one note, one task”
When the calendar block starts:
1) Open the **Main Project Hub** note.
2) Open **Today (Shortlist)**.
3) Work only on the MINA until the timer ends.

If you get distracted, do this:
- Write the distracting thought into a mini section in the note: **“Parking Lot”**
- Return to the task.

**Finish line for the block:** produce something tangible (a paragraph, solved exercise set, code commit, slide, outline, etc.).

---

### End of day (10 minutes): “Reset”
In this order:
1) In Notes (Main Project Hub): write **1–3 bullets**: what moved today.
2) In Reminders:  
   - Clear **Today (Shortlist)** (complete or move back).  
   - Pick tomorrow’s MINA and put it in **Today (Shortlist)** *only if you want to wake up with it ready*.
3) In Calendar: if tomorrow is messy, **move** the deep work block now.

This makes consistency easier than motivation.

---

## 4) Weekly rhythm (20 minutes, once)
Pick one day. Put a recurring event: **Weekly Review (20 min)**.

Checklist:
- In Notes: update “This Week (1–3 outcomes)”
- In Reminders: prune Main Project list (keep it executable)
- In Calendar: block **3 deep work sessions** for the week (even if you’ll move them)

Don’t aim for 7 perfect days; aim for **3–5 deep sessions/week**.

## 5) How you break the project into “finishable” steps
Your attention will cooperate more if tasks are sized right.

Use this rule for any task that feels heavy:
- Convert to a next action that starts with a verb and ends with a deliverable.

Examples:
- “Work on website” → “Write homepage outline (H1 + 5 sections)”
- “Study ML” → “Complete lesson 3 + write 5-bullet summary”
- “Build feature” → “Implement endpoint + return mock data”

If a task can’t be done in **<90 minutes**, split it.
